scenario_summary: A journey through the world of permutations and combinations, using abstract mathematical concepts to solve real-world problems.
visual_setting: A clean, dark background with mathematical notation, geometric primitives, and clean text labels.

scenes.title: Understanding Permutations
scenes.narration: In permutations, the order of arrangement matters. For example, how many ways can we arrange 3 digits from 1 to 9?
scenes.animation_description: Three circles labeled 1, 2, 3 appear. An arrow points to the first circle, indicating the first position.
scenes.manim_hint: Use the `Permutation` class to demonstrate the arrangement of items.

scenes.title: Calculating Permutations
scenes.narration: To find the number of permutations, we use the formula nPn = n!.
scenes.animation_description: The formula nPn = n! appears, with n = 9. An arrow points to the factorial symbol.

scenes.title: No Repeated Digits
scenes.narration: When no digit is repeated, we calculate permutations using nPn.
scenes.animation_description: The formula nPn = n! reappears. An arrow points to the variable n.

scenes.title: Calculating Permutations with No Repeats
scenes.narration: For 3 digits from 1 to 9, the number of permutations is 9P3 = 9! / (9-3)! = 720.
scenes.animation_description: The formula 9P3 = 9! / (9-3)! appears. The result 720 is displayed.
scenes.manim_hint: Calculate the factorial using `MathTex` and display the result.

scenes.title: Permutations with Specific Conditions
scenes.narration: How many 3-digit even numbers can be made using 1, 2, 3, 4, 6, 7 without repetition?
scenes.animation_description: Six circles labeled 1, 2, 3, 4, 6, 7 appear. An arrow points to the circle labeled 2, indicating it must be the last digit for the number to be even.
scenes.manim_hint: Use the `Permutation` class to demonstrate the arrangement of items with a condition.

scenes.title: Calculating Permutations with Conditions
scenes.narration: For the last digit to be even, we have 3 choices (2, 4, 6). The remaining two digits can be arranged in 5P2 ways.
scenes.animation_description: The formula 3 * 5P2 appears. The result 30 is displayed.
scenes.manim_hint: Calculate the factorial using `MathTex` and display the result.

scenes.title: Combinations
scenes.narration: Combinations are used when the order does not matter. For example, how many ways can we choose 4 letters from the word 'EQUATION'?
scenes.animation_description: The word 'EQUATION' is displayed. Four circles labeled E, Q, U, A, T, I, O, N appear. An arrow points to the first circle, indicating the first selection.
scenes.manim_hint: Use the `CombinatorialObject` class to demonstrate the selection of items.

scenes.title: Calculating Combinations
scenes.narration: To find the number of combinations, we use the formula nCr = n! / (r!(n-r)!)
scenes.animation_description: The formula nCr = n! / (r!(n-r)!) appears, with n = 8 and r = 4. An arrow points to the factorial symbol.

scenes.title: Combinations with Conditions
scenes.narration: How many words can be formed using all letters of 'EQUATION' without repetition?
scenes.animation_description: The word 'EQUATION' is displayed. Eight circles labeled E, Q, U, A, T, I, O, N appear. An arrow points to the first circle, indicating the first selection.
scenes.manim_hint: Use the `CombinatorialObject` class to demonstrate the selection of items with no repetition.

scenes.title: Calculating Combinations with Conditions
scenes.narration: The number of words is given by 8C8 = 1.
scenes.animation_description: The formula 8C8 = 1 appears. The result 1 is displayed.
scenes.manim_hint: Calculate the combination using `MathTex` and display the result.

scenes.title: Recap
scenes.narration: We learned about permutations and combinations, and how to calculate them using formulas. We also explored how to apply these concepts to real-world problems.
scenes.animation_description: A recap slide with key formulas and concepts appears.
scenes.manim_hint: Use a `Text` object to display the recap content.
